articleTitle: Developing guidelines for object oriented user interfaces
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Progress in Object Technology
abstract: The author discusses the change to an object-oriented user interface and some implementation problems. He considers how object oriented user interfaces gain most power when the user can assemble parts to make useful objects. Each part can be tuned to handling or displaying a particular type of data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some principles for the encapsulation of the behaviour of aggregate objects
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Progress in Object Technology
abstract: In this paper, a framework is proposed for the analysis of systems of objects which exhibit state-based behaviour and multiple inheritance of that behaviour within class hierarchies. The approach proposed is based on a graphical notation which could form the basis for recursive analysis or synthesis of system specifications. Whilst suitable for communication between analyst and client, the notation should be amenable also both to reasoning and to CASE support.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Case study: implementing an object-oriented design in C++
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Progress in Object Technology
abstract: Many object-oriented methodologies give the impression that the process of taking a completed design and implementing it is mechanistic, even trivial. Instead software engineers find in practice that there are a large number of decisions still to be taken even after the specification and design are complete. This is particularly true when the implementation language for the product is designed to allow the widest possible range of implementation choices; so it is particularly true when the implementation language is C++. This paper describes some of the implementation issues faced by one project, and examines some of the additional personal role that aided their resolution. The project under development was an embedded system performing protocol conversion and database caching, part of a network management system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Architecture and maintenance in object technology
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Progress in Object Technology
abstract: In order to explore the impact of different architectures on software maintenance, we took the following approach: write two versions of the same application with differing architectures; implement the same specific changes to both versions; measure the cost of making each change using simple metrics; and compare the costs of each change between architectures, and also within the same architecture. For our example we chose a simple banking application which must operate on a number of different kinds of account.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design of neural networks with object oriented techniques
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Recent Progress in Object Technology
abstract: This paper describes the use of object oriented technology applied to the design of neural networks. Aspects of code probability and reusability were a major motivation for using this technology because several different network architectures were being investigated. It is necessary to focus on characteristics common to most neural architectures and to abstract these as the basis of the design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
